definitions.gloss: to accompany, to stay close to, to attend
definitions.explanation: To stay close beside someone in a supportive or caring role. Often implies watching over, assisting, or keeping someone company, especially during illness or difficulty.
To become husband and wife, to live together as a married couple. A somewhat literary or traditional way to express marriage, often seen in the pattern {連|つ}れ{添|そ}う (to live together as spouses).

examples.english: To stay by a sick person's side.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{入院中|にゅういんちゅう}の{父|ちち}にずっと{添|そ}っていた。
examples.english: My mother stayed at the side of my hospitalized father the whole time.

examples.japanese: {付|つ}き{添|そ}いの{人|ひと}がいないと{不安|ふあん}だ。
examples.english: I feel uneasy without someone to accompany me.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{若|わか}くして{添|そ}った。
{長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{夫婦|ふうふ}だ。
examples.english: They are a couple who have been together for many years.

examples.japanese: {好|す}きな{人|ひと}と{添|そ}い{遂|と}げたいと{願|ねが}っている。
examples.english: I wish to spend my whole life with the person I love.

notes:
USAGE:
Not to be confused with the homophone {沿|そ}う (to run along, to follow a path/policy). {添|そ}う emphasizes personal closeness and caring support, while {沿|そ}う means to follow alongside something like a road or guideline.

The marriage sense is somewhat literary and traditional. In modern Japanese, {結婚|けっこん}する is more common for "to marry," but {添|そ}う and its compounds remain widely understood.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {付|つ}き{添|そ}う: to accompany, to attend (someone)
- {付|つ}き{添|そ}い: attendant, escort, chaperone
- {連|つ}れ{添|そ}う: to live together as a married couple
- {添|そ}い{遂|と}げる: to remain married until the end, to grow old together
- {寄|よ}り{添|そ}う: to snuggle up to, to stay close (emotionally or physically)
